sqlite.writer: one extension-host writer connection owned by the SQLite adapter
sqlite.readers: bounded read-only connections; every query observes one committed snapshot
sqlite.busyPolicy: retry reads with bounded jitter; retry a write transaction at most three times before temporarily-unavailable; never retry after external effect handoff
integrity: PRAGMA foreign_key_check on activation and after migration
PRAGMA integrity_check before and after backup restore, after migration, and when corruption is suspected
sqlite.crashRule: an incomplete SQLite transaction rolls back; committed state is authoritative; any effect with intent committed but no known outcome is reconciled before replay

columnTypes.id: TEXT containing a canonical 128-scalar-value maximum identity
columnTypes.version: INTEGER >= 1, incremented exactly once per accepted aggregate mutation
columnTypes.instant: TEXT UTC RFC3339 with millisecond precision
columnTypes.json: TEXT canonical JSON validated by the adapter against a named closed schema

tables.name: artifacts
constraints: relative_key is adapter-generated beneath private workspace storage and contains no absolute path or traversal
tables.lifecycle: immutable bytes; deletion only after no live typed reference and retention eligibility

tables.name: application_operations
constraints: accepted requires result_json, transaction_id, and completed_at
tables.lifecycle: retained with the owning authoritative object; exact duplicate returns the recorded result

tables.name: tasks
constraints: state is a canonical WF-019 Task state
continuation IS NULL OR continuation IN ('preparing','running','verifying')
queue_ordinal is non-null only for queued Tasks and is unique when non-null
terminal_at is present exactly for terminal states
tables.lifecycle: soft Trash only after terminal; authoritative history survives Trash; reset is the only bulk destruction

tables.name: task_dependencies
constraints: accepted edge requires succeeded prerequisite for active context

tables.name: dependency_requests
constraints: UNIQUE(task_id, candidate_task_id, contract_version, context) WHERE status='open'
resolved_at is present exactly when status is not open

tables.name: task_graph_revisions
constraints: Task and contract foreign keys RESTRICT

tables.name: subtasks
constraints: FOREIGN KEY(task_id, created_revision) REFERENCES task_graph_revisions(task_id, revision) RESTRICT
state is a canonical WF-019 Subtask state
superseded only from pending or ready

tables.name: subtask_dependencies
constraints: revision and both Subtask foreign keys RESTRICT

tables.name: task_blockers

tables.name: task_amendments

tables.name: repair_cycles

tables.name: unsatisfiable_determinations

tables.name: chat_sessions

surviving forks RESTRICT parent permanent deletion until shared items are materialized or all child references are absent
trashed Sessions are excluded from ordinary lists but remain authoritative

tables.name: chat_turns
constraints: Chat and Artifact foreign keys RESTRICT
immutable; redaction replaces referenced artifact with a tombstone artifact through an audited operation

tables.name: response_attempts
constraints: Chat, Turn, Resource Snapshot, and Artifact foreign keys RESTRICT

at most one nonterminal attempt per Chat
terminal attempts are append-only and never resumed

tables.name: chat_outputs
constraints: Attempt and Artifact foreign keys RESTRICT

tables.name: chat_summaries
constraints: Chat and Artifact foreign keys RESTRICT

tables.name: chat_ledger_entries

tables.name: chat_context_pins

tables.name: resource_snapshot_entries

tables.name: authority_reviews
constraints: one open review per owner and logical scope

tables.name: authority_grants
constraints: Review and Snapshot foreign keys RESTRICT
scope is never broader than approved review

tables.name: mcp_trust

tables.name: durable_operations

Authority, Snapshot, and Artifact foreign keys RESTRICT

tables.name: operation_execution_attempts

tables.name: operation_barriers

tables.name: reconciliation_evidence

tables.name: durable_checkpoints

tables.name: tool_audit_records
constraints: Operation and Review foreign keys RESTRICT

tables.name: tool_audit_corrections

tables.name: memory_proposals

tables.name: memory_proposal_sources
constraints: Proposal and provenance foreign keys RESTRICT

tables.name: memory_proposal_targets

tables.name: memory_provenance

tables.name: memory_conflicts

tables.name: operational_incidents

tables.name: domain_events

tables.name: lifecycle_event_identities

tables.name: rejection_records

tables.name: active_task_slot

tables.name: repository_write_lock

tables.name: assignment_capacity_leases

tables.name: chat_mutation_capacity

tables.name: recovery_steps

tables.name: backups

crossRecordTriggers: task_dependencies and subtask_dependencies reject cycles through recursive CTE guards

Task terminal entry rejects an Active Task Slot, Repository Write Lock, open blocker, unresolved dependency/routing request, nonterminal or outcome-unknown operation, or missing required success/failure evidence
Active Task Slot insertion and removal validate canonical Task state boundaries
Repository Write Lock insertion requires the same Active Task Slot owner and an executing phase; deletion is paired with the Task transition
assignment_capacity_leases enforces three total and one write-capable owner
chat_mutation_capacity requires no Repository Write Lock and one executing mutation operation
Task, Subtask, Assignment Attempt, Response Attempt, Durable Operation, compatibility, and migration updates validate the exact WF-019 transition matrix
aggregate version updates require OLD.version + 1 and one matching domain_events row in the same application transaction
append-only tables reject UPDATE and DELETE outside the migration/reset connection capability
typed artifact foreign keys are RESTRICT; no reference is cleared until replacement or owner retention allows it

artifactPolicy.inline: identities, enums, bounded summaries, hashes, counters, timestamps, repository-relative path tokens, and closed sanitized metadata JSON only
artifactPolicy.artifactBacked: user prompts, model output, diffs, file bodies, Tool input/results that may contain content, checkpoint continuation bodies, Memory replacements, migration/support evidence, and Support Bundles
artifactPolicy.identity: opaque Artifact ID plus adapter-generated private relative key, SHA-256, byte length, media type, and classification
artifactPolicy.writeProtocol: write temp file, fsync, hash and length verify, atomically rename, then commit the typed SQLite reference; a pre-reference crash leaves an unreferenced candidate
artifactPolicy.readProtocol: resolve only through adapter; verify relative containment, length, and SHA-256 before use
artifactPolicy.orphanCleanup: after startup recovery and daily at most, delete temp files older than 24 hours and immutable artifacts with no typed reference and delete_after elapsed; never delete a referenced, pinned, or backup file
artifactPolicy.secrets: credential values and raw secrets remain in SecretStorage or provider-owned flows; SQLite may hold only opaque handles and non-revealing fingerprints

retention.taskAndChat: Trash is a visibility state, not deletion; authoritative history survives Trash. Permanent Chat deletion requires terminal Attempts, no reconciling/outcome-unknown operation, no pinned diagnostic evidence, and no surviving fork reference.
retention.forks: a fork is an independent Chat aggregate referencing immutable source items through its fork point; it survives source Trash. Source permanent deletion is RESTRICTed until shared history is materialized into the fork or the fork is deleted.
retention.audit: Tool Audit, operation, checkpoint, authority, and application-operation records follow the owning Task or Chat and are not removed by diagnostic cleanup.
retention.diagnostics: ordinary events expire at 30 days or when total stored diagnostic bytes exceed 50 MiB; oldest unpinned first. Resolved pins expire no earlier than 30 days after resolution.
retention.reset: workbench.data.reset is the only command allowed to destroy all workspace operational records and private artifacts; it preserves only an external sanitized reset audit/incident if the live database is replaced.

transactionProfiles.stateEvent: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; validate compatibility, expected versions, lifecycle and authority; insert application_operations accepted row; mutate owned aggregate and dependent rows; append exactly ordered domain_events and required audit/attention/diagnostic facts; store result; COMMIT
transactionProfiles.intentBeforeEffect: transaction A records immutable Durable Operation intent, Operation Key, authority and Tool audit plus operation.intent-recorded; external effect occurs only after commit; transaction B records known outcome or reconciliation state, audit evidence, caller state/checkpoint and events
transactionProfiles.externalPreparation: commit proposal/preview/interaction state and event; perform native UI or read-only discovery outside the transaction; commit returned metadata or failure in a new stateEvent transaction
transactionProfiles.readOnlyExternal: no authoritative SQLite state or Domain Event; native UI action may emit only redacted ephemeral diagnostics
transactionProfiles.compatibilityExternal: uses the compatibility/recovery connection while Runtime writes are disabled; record intent outside the live database when it is unsafe, execute backup/restore/fresh operation, then reopen at checking; never pretend atomicity across filesystem replacement
transactionProfiles.destructiveReset: close Runtime connections, record exact confirmed recovery action, atomically move live database and artifact root to a private Trash location, create and verify a fresh v1 store, then delete old data only after reopen success

recoveryActions.name: activation.recover
recoveryActions.rule: persist run/worklist first; each deterministic step is its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction

recoveryActions.name: operation.reconcile
recoveryActions.rule: classification and resulting operation/barrier/audit event commit together

recoveryActions.name: checkpoint.restore
recoveryActions.rule: restored continuation or explicit blocker and recovery progress commit together

recoveryActions.name: migration.apply
recoveryActions.rule: the full ordered chain and target verification run in one exclusive migration transaction after verified backup

recoveryActions.name: backup.restore
recoveryActions.rule: live database replacement is filesystem-atomic, externally audited, followed by checking; no Runtime write transaction spans replacement

recoveryActions.name: artifact.orphan-cleanup
recoveryActions.rule: select eligible unreferenced rows in a snapshot, delete files idempotently, then delete metadata in a short BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; failure leaves retryable metadata

schemaAssertions: every table, column, foreign key, unique key, check, index, and trigger is generated from this contract and introspected from a migrated database
all aggregate state enums and transition triggers equal the WF-019 lifecycle catalog
all event names and payload schema identifiers equal the WF-020 protocol catalog
every WF-020 state-changing command occurs exactly once in commandMap and every read-only command is explicitly classified
all artifact reference columns are included in the orphan-reference union
all append-only tables reject unauthorized update and delete
faultInjection: before BEGIN, after each row write, before COMMIT, after COMMIT, before effect handoff, during effect, before outcome commit, and after outcome commit
WAL busy/locked, disk full, artifact short write, checksum mismatch, corrupt page, foreign-key violation, trigger rejection, host termination, stale lease, and migration reopen failure
verification.requiredOutcomes: committed state/event/audit agree, or the transaction is absent; external effects are known or blocked behind reconciliation; no impossible lease, lifecycle, graph, fork, retention, or artifact state becomes writable
